hook: SCP-2293 opens as a sober report on a phenomenon that slips one identical line about Stephen King's 1999 car accident into books, albums and broadcasts. The bulk of the file, though, is a recovered group chat, crammed with swearing, typos and in-jokes, and that is where the actual story happens. It's a comedy piece, so read it for the voices.
whyItMatters:
This is a joke article that commits completely to its gag. The containment section authorizes the destruction of whole areas over a single non sequitur, and the falling Hume levels give the joke real weight inside the setting.

It also lets a Group of Interest, GoI-5869 or Gamers Against Weed, introduce itself in its own words: each member of the chat has a distinct voice, from the calm moderator to the one who can barely type.
thingsToNotice: The report's dry details set up the punchline, since King's own books, his Bachman pseudonym and adaptations of his work are all immune, and the task force sent after it is nicknamed Bachman's Boys. In the log, bluntfiend keeps quoting the line as a joke while the others talk about a new It movie, gaycopmp4 objects because King nearly died, and bluntfiend apologizes, only for gaycopmp4 to return furious a little later. The line has invaded Game of Thrones right before a beheading, a Final Fantasy XII cutscene on every replay and save file, and even a Beatles CD belonging to gaycopmp4's mother. bones makes bluntfiend apologize, and the matter seems closed until someone shares a Reddit thread in which Alec Baldwin, playing Donald Trump on Saturday Night Live, turns to camera and delivers the same trivia. bluntfiend's only defense is that a good joke wants an audience, and when the thread vanishes almost at once, the chat jokes that the janitors must have been called, a sign that the prank has slipped out of its maker's hands.

related.note: A footnote names the same group as a suspect in this earlier case.
